teaser: Every project should budget for maintaining the platforms it runs on, sized to it and visible monthly; a month of php2shell data shows the gap.
core_idea: Maintaining the core open source platforms should be a recurring, proportional cost item in every project's own budget, paid to people connected to the code and visible as work every month, with its absence a named risk; the NCSC-NL php2shell inventory four weeks on shows 543 of 976 entries with no fix or clean status.

nodes.label: The cost item
nodes.summary: A line in every project budget.

nodes.label: 240 runtime-dependent
nodes.summary: Whoever runs PHP answers for it.

nodes.label: Down the chain
nodes.summary: Maintainers paid to help build on top.

quotes.text: Each is a different way of saying that nobody was paid to know.
This is the line I am proposing, already being paid in risk.
A flat sponsorship from a central budget does not move when one project doubles; a line inside the project does.
